enriched.summary: A aula aborda aspectos gramaticais, vocabulário e pronúncia relacionados a adjetivos, verbos irregulares e expressões do dia a dia. Os exemplos práticos destacam o uso de tempos verbais como Simple Past, Past Continuous e Future, além de introduzir palavras e expressões úteis para situações cotidianas.
mainTopics: Tempos verbais (Simple Past, Past Continuous, Future)

vocabulary.definition: Used to add emphasis to adjectives or adverbs.
examples: The boat is very close to sinking.
Lucy and Chris are very far away from the gas station.

vocabulary.definition: To go down below the surface of water, mud, etc.
examples: The boat is going to sink because there is a hole in the bottom and a lot of water is getting in.
The Titanic sank in 1912.
Oliver and I are going to play tennis on the weekend if his knee is already well.
She felt sick after eating too much.

vocabulary.definition: An opening or hollow space in something.
examples: The boat is going to sink because there is a hole in the bottom.
He dug a hole in the garden to plant a tree.

vocabulary.definition: To have no more of something left.
examples: Lucy and Chris are going to run out of gas because there is very little gas in the tank.
We ran out of sugar while baking the cake.

vocabulary.definition: The joint between the thigh and the lower leg.
examples: Oliver and I are going to play tennis on the weekend if his knee is already well.
He injured his knee during the game.

vocabulary.definition: A device that makes things visible, or a source of illumination.
examples: You must stop when the traffic light is red.
The light in the room was very dim.

vocabulary.definition: Comparative form of 'old'; having lived for more years.
examples: He is older than his brother.
This building is older than the school.

vocabulary.definition: Superlative form of 'old'; having lived the most years.
examples: She is the oldest in her family.
This is the oldest tree in the park.

grammar.explanation: Used to describe completed actions that happened in the past.
rules: Regular verbs add '-ed' to the base form.
Irregular verbs have unique past forms.
examples: I met Tom and Jane at the airport.
He met his wife when he was working in Japan.
commonMistakes: Using present tense instead of past (e.g., 'I meet Tom yesterday' instead of 'I met Tom yesterday').

grammar.explanation: Used to talk about plans or intentions and predictions based on evidence.
rules: Use 'not' to form the negative (e.g., 'is not going to').
examples: The boat is going to sink.
Lucy and Chris are going to run out of gas.
commonMistakes: Omitting 'to' (e.g., 'I am going play' instead of 'I am going to play').
Using 'will' instead of 'going to' for plans.

expressions.meaning: To have no more of something left.
expressions.usage: Used to describe depletion of resources.
examples: Lucy and Chris are going to run out of gas because there is very little gas in the tank.

expressions.meaning: To be in a rush or to do something quickly.
expressions.usage: Commonly used when someone has limited time.
examples: She left in a hurry without saying goodbye.

practiceQuestions.question: Complete the sentence: Lucy and Chris are going to ___ gas because there is very little in the tank.
practiceQuestions.explanation: 'Run out of' means to deplete or have no more of something.

practiceQuestions.question: What is the past form of 'sink'?
practiceQuestions.explanation: 'Sink' is an irregular verb; its past form is 'sank'.

culturalNotes: Expressions like 'run out of' are commonly used in everyday English to describe practical situations.
Understanding verb tenses is crucial for clear communication in English.
studyTips: Practice conjugating irregular verbs daily to internalize their forms.
Use flashcards to memorize vocabulary and their translations.
Incorporate new expressions into your daily conversations to reinforce learning.
originalExamples: The boat is going to sink because there is a hole in the bottom and a lot of water is getting in. (O barco vai afundar porque tem um buraco no fundo e muita água está entrando.)

Lucy and Chris are going to run out of gas because there is very little gas in the tank and the nearest gas station is very far away. (Lucy e Chris vão ficar sem gasolina porque tem muito pouca gasolina no tanque e o posto de gasolina mais próximo fica muito longe.)
Oliver and I are going to play tennis on the weekend if his knee is already well. (Oliver e eu vamos jogar tênis no final de semana se o joelho dele já estiver bem.)
I’ve heard that you received a job offer but you aren’t going to accept it. (Ouvi dizer que você recebeu uma proposta de trabalho mas não vai aceitá-la.)
My grandmother is going to bring that delicious dessert that only she knows how to make. (Minha avó vai trazer aquela sobremesa deliciosa que só ela sabe fazer.)
